updateCadence: Roughly every 1-3 months, mostly Chromium/Electron updates
summary: Min is a lightweight Electron-based browser with a unified search/address bar, tasks (tab groups), tracker and ad blocking, reader view and userscripts. It has no extension store or sync, but 1.35 added local page translation via Bergamot.
bestFor: People wanting a clean, simple browser with built-in blocking
Raspberry Pi and older desktop use
Privacy-minded users who do not need extensions
notFor: People who rely on browser extensions or sync
Users who need frequent security patching

pros.title: Clean, fast UI
pros.detail: Unified search bar and "tasks" grouping keep the interface small.

pros.title: Built-in blocking
pros.detail: Ad and tracker blocking, plus image/script blocking, without extensions.

pros.title: Local translation
pros.detail: Version 1.35.0 runs page translation locally via Bergamot.

pros.title: Userscripts and reader view
pros.detail: Supports userscripts and automatic reader view.

pros.title: No telemetry
pros.detail: Open source (Apache-2.0) and does not phone home.

cons.title: No extensions or sync
cons.detail: No extension support and no cross-device sync.

cons.title: Electron overhead
cons.detail: Memory and startup are not much better than mainstream Chromium browsers.

cons.title: Slow patch rhythm
cons.detail: Chromium bumps appeared roughly every 1-3 months in the 1.35.x series.

cons.title: Small maintainer base
cons.detail: Release history shows long gaps (e.g. none between Oct 2025 and Jan 2026).

faq.a: No. It supports userscripts but not Chrome Web Store extensions.

privacyDefaults: Blocking on by default; no telemetry
productivity: Reader view, bookmark search, PDF viewer
businessTrust: No business model, small maintainer team

featureNotes.commandBar: Unified bar with bangs and shortcuts
